observations.text: SP, at the desired standard for this stage, executed the cross under following the leader's command with the IP directing the initial power reduction and the stack-down. Lateral spacing was kept within one A/C length and no closer than 10 feet to No1, and the flight path stayed clear of the leader's prop wash. Marginal performance for the Training Section - self-initiated timing of the position change is expected to improve on the next sortie.

SP initiated the position change on the leader's command and completed the cross under with the IP's verbal directives only, without IP intervention on the controls. Airspeed split against No1 stayed at the 20 knot limit and the exit heading was regained within 10 degrees, with no entry into the leader's prop wash. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the position change timely on the leader's command, passing clear of the leader's prop wash and never closer than 10 feet to No1. Deviations peaked at 200 feet from the briefed formation altitude and 15 knots of airspeed, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the cross under timely and correctly on the leader's command, holding a stepped-down flight path clear of the leader's prop wash. Lateral movement was smooth, continuous and solid, spacing never exceeded one A/C length and never closed inside 10 feet of No1, while altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the position change with excellent accuracy, initiating on the leader's command and repositioning in a smooth, continuous and solid manner without any IP intervention. Deviations were negligible - within 30 feet of altitude, 3 knots of airspeed and 2 degrees on the exit heading - with constant spacing inside one A/C length and safe clearance from both No1 and the leader's prop wash. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an untimely and excessive power reduction at the start of the position change, did not establish the stepped-down flight path required to pass clear of the leader, with the result that the A/C flew into the leader's prop wash and the IP took the controls to reposition it. Airspeed split reached 30 knots below No1, beyond the 20 knot limit. The cross under could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not arrest the lateral movement toward No1 during the cross under, with the result that the A/C approached the leader closer than 10 feet and the IP intervened on the controls to open the spacing. Recovery of the briefed position was directed by the IP throughout.

SP executed the position change at the desired standard for this stage, completing the cross under after the IP's verbal directives on power setting and stack-down. Deviations reached the 300 feet altitude and 20 knots airspeed limits and were recognized and corrected with delay, but without IP intervention on the controls. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timeliness of the initial power reduction is expected to improve.

SP executed the position change timely on the leader's command, passing clear of the leader's prop wash and holding spacing within one A/C length. Small errors in power control produced a maximum of 180 feet of altitude deviation and 13 knots of airspeed difference, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention or verbal prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the cross under timely and correctly on the leader's command, without the necessity for IP intervention. Control of the A/C was smooth, continuous and solid, spacing remained within one A/C length and never closer than 10 feet to No1, with altitude held within 120 feet, airspeed within 7 knots and exit heading within 4 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the position change with exceptional accuracy, initiating immediately on the leader's command and crossing under in a smooth, continuous and solid manner. Altitude, airspeed and exit heading deviations were negligible at 30 feet, 3 knots and 1 degree respectively, with constant clearance from the leader's prop wash and no approach inside 10 feet of No1. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient stack-down before initiating the lateral movement, did not keep the flight path below the leader during the cross under, with the result that the A/C entered the leader's prop wash and departed the briefed formation altitude by 400 feet. The IP took the controls to reposition the A/C on the new side. The position change was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not execute the position change timely on the leader's command and lost visual reference to No1 during the crossing. Spacing opened to more than three A/C lengths and airspeed fell 25 knots below the leader, with the result that the IP directed the rejoin and executed part of the repositioning. Recognition of the deviation came only after the IP's call.

SP, due to a delayed and insufficient power addition after passing under the leader, did not arrest the aft drift during the position change, with the result that the airspeed split reached 20 knots and spacing opened to the maximum of one A/C length. The correct position was regained only after the IP's verbal directives, the error being recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the observed aircraft performance did not match the expected, did not question the increasing vertical displacement while crossing under No1 and continued the movement unchanged. Altitude deviation from the briefed formation altitude reached 300 feet and the exit heading was 10 degrees off the leader's. Both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts, without IP intervention on the controls.

SP executed the position change on the leader's command within the desired standards, keeping clear of the leader's prop wash and no closer than 10 feet to No1. Small errors in power management twice produced deviations of about 200 feet in altitude and 14 knots in airspeed, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoothness and continuity of the crossing are expected to improve with repetition.

SP executed the cross under timely and correctly on the leader's command, without the necessity for IP intervention. Spacing was held within one A/C length, clear of the leader's prop wash and never inside 10 feet of No1, with altitude within 110 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and exit heading within 5 degrees. Control of the A/C was smooth, continuous and solid throughout the position change. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the position change with exceptional accuracy and speed, initiating on the leader's command and repositioning in a smooth, continuous and solid manner. Deviations were negligible at 25 feet of altitude, 2 knots of airspeed and 1 degree of exit heading, with stable clearance from No1 and no contact with the leader's prop wash. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an over-controlled lateral input at the start of the cross under, did not control the A/C in a smooth, continuous and solid manner and generated closure toward No1. The A/C approached the leader closer than 10 feet and the IP intervened on the controls to open the spacing. The position change could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to degraded situational awareness after the unplanned change of sequence, did not execute the position change timely on the leader's command and began the crossing while still stepped up. The A/C flew through the leader's prop wash and diverged 450 feet from the briefed formation altitude, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and executed part of the repositioning. The deviation was not recognized before the IP's call.

SP, due to an insufficient initial power reduction, did not establish the stack-down required before moving laterally, with the result that the A/C skimmed the edge of the leader's prop wash and the airspeed split reached 20 knots. The new position was established only after the IP's verbal directives, the error being recognized and corrected with delay, without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments while attention remained fixed on No1, did not hold the briefed formation altitude and exit heading during the cross under. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and the exit heading 10 degrees off the leader's, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of both deviations was delayed.

SP, due to a slightly late power addition on regaining the new position, did not stop the aft drift immediately after passing under the leader, with the result that spacing momentarily opened beyond one A/C length and the airspeed split reached 14 knots. The deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention.

SP, due to workload distribution that left the SP flying and transmitting at the same time, did not begin the position change immediately on the leader's command and allowed the flight path to rise during the crossing. Altitude deviation from the briefed formation altitude reached 190 feet and the exit heading 7 degrees, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Clearance from No1 remained greater than 10 feet throughout.

SP executed the cross under timely and correctly on the leader's command, without the necessity for IP intervention, keeping spacing within one A/C length and clear of the leader's prop wash. Altitude was held within 140 feet and airspeed within 9 knots, close to the limits of the desired standard, and two crossings required small corrective inputs to keep the movement continuous. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoothness and solidity of control during the crossing are expected to improve.

SP executed the position change with exceptional accuracy and speed, initiating immediately on the leader's command and crossing under in a smooth, continuous and solid manner in both closed and route formation. Deviations were negligible at 25 feet of altitude, 2 knots of airspeed and 1 degree of exit heading, with stable spacing well inside one A/C length and constant clearance from No1 and from the leader's prop wash. Above end of block MIF achieved.
